messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Nimble in RStudio?
parts:
Hi Nimble-users,

I see that the manual suggests to 'turn off the option to display the global environment' but I'm not quite clear what that means.  (Seems I am not alone either: https://support.rstudio.com/hc/communities/public/questions/201403153-is-it-possible-not-to-display-the-global-environment). I can minimize the global environment but do not see a way to 'turn it off'.  Even with it minimized RStudio seems to hang when simply running the pump example (chapter 2 in the manual). Outside of RStudio things seem fine.

Thanks,

Carl

messages.author: 99aa11b224ba9e9e
messages.subject: Re: Nimble in RStudio?
parts:
Carl, thanks for raising this issue.  Let me explain, in detail, what I've done to get NIMBLE working in RStudio, on Windows.

First, I'm running 64-bit Windows 7 Enterprise edition, RStudio version 0.98.932, and R version 3.1.2 (Pumpkin Helmet).

The RStudio GUI has four major panes.
Exactly what appears in each of these is customizable via menu item Tools > Global Options > Pane Layout, then a series of drop-down menus and check boxes.
However, regardless of how you customize it, the "Environment" display will necessarily appear in one of these panes.
To explain by example, I'll leave Environment coupled (in the same pane) along with History, Packages, and Viewer.

Now, back to RStudio.
In that pane containing Environment, History, Packages, and Viewer, there are 4 tabs corresponding to these views.
To get NIMBLE working, it **does not matter** which of these tabs is clicked.  You may as well just leave it displaying the Environment tab, in this pane.

Looking at this pane, the top line has the 4 tabs (Environment, History, Packages, Viewer).
The next line below that has some little icons: a folder, a disc, "import dataset", a broom, etc..
The next line below that -- this one is the key! -- on the far left, there's clickable text with a small downward arrow, selecting *which* environment/package/namespace contents to display.
If this is left on the default selection "Global Environment", then NIMBLE will hang, essentially right when you create the first NIMBLE model object.
If you click this text, opening a drop-down menu, and select "package:stats" (that's what I leave mine on), then it will display the contents of that package -- not any of the NIMBLE objects.
Now, NIMBLE should work fine.
Just don't ever change that back to "Global Environment".

Please let me know if this isn't clear in any way.  Or, if it solves the problem for you!

Good luck,
Daniel
NIMBLE Development Team
